Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR questions. TWO questions must be chosen from SECTION A, ONE from SECTION B and ONE other from SECTION C. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

questions.enonce_markdown:
What were the main reasons for the creation of ECOWAS in 1975? Describe the functioning of any two organs of ECOWAS. How far has ECOWAS been successful in solving the economic problems of the West African sub region?

(8/6/6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** ECOWAS (the Economic Community of West African States) was created by the Treaty of Lagos on 28 May 1975, signed by fifteen West African states (including Nigeria, Ghana, Togo, Senegal, Ivory Coast and others); Cape Verde joined in 1977. Its headquarters are at Abuja. Its aim is the economic integration of the region.

**(a) Reasons for the creation of ECOWAS [8 marks].**
1. *To create a larger market.* Most West African states are small and poor, with small domestic markets; union would allow trade across borders and economies of scale.
2. *To promote economic development and self-reliance.* The leaders wanted to reduce dependence on the former colonial powers and on the export of raw materials, and to develop industry and agriculture together (collective self-reliance).
3. *To remove the effects of colonial boundaries.* Colonial borders had cut across peoples and economies and separated English-speaking, French-speaking and Portuguese-speaking states, so integration would bring them together.
4. *To develop common infrastructure,* such as roads, telecommunications, energy and transport links between states.
5. *To abolish barriers to trade and to the movement of persons, capital and services* (customs duties, quotas, visas).
6. *The influence of Pan-Africanism and of the Organisation of African Unity (OAU),* which encouraged regional groupings; the example of the European Economic Community and the Francophone groupings such as the CEAO (1973), which showed that the English-speaking states had to be part of a wider body.
7. *The leadership of Nigeria and Togo.* Nigeria, with oil wealth and the largest population, and Togo, under General Eyadema, promoted the idea.
8. *Common problems.* Poverty, drought, food shortage and unemployment were seen as problems that were better solved together.

**(b) Functioning of two organs [6 marks].**
1. *The Authority of Heads of State and Government.* It is the supreme institution. It meets at least once a year, decides the general policy and direction of the Community, gives instructions to the other institutions, appoints the top officials, and amends the treaty. The chairman changes each year.
2. *The Council of Ministers.* It consists of the ministers of each member state (usually the ministers in charge of ECOWAS affairs or foreign affairs). It meets before the summit and twice a year, supervises the work of the Community, prepares the budget and the recommendations for the Authority and makes decisions on the implementation of the Authority's policies.
3. *Other organs* that can be used: the Executive Secretariat (later the Commission, at Abuja) which carries out the decisions, headed by an Executive Secretary (President of the Commission); the Community Court of Justice, which settles disputes about the treaty; the Community Parliament; the ECOWAS Fund for Co-operation, Compensation and Development (later the Bank for Investment and Development), which finances projects and compensates members for losses.
Note: the revised treaty of 1993 (Cotonou) strengthened the institutions and added the Parliament and the Court.

**(c) How far ECOWAS has succeeded economically [6 marks].**
*Achievements.*
1. The *Protocol on Free Movement of Persons* (1979) gave citizens the right to enter, reside and set up businesses in other member states without a visa for a limited period; there is an ECOWAS passport and the Brown Card motor-insurance scheme.
2. A *trade liberalisation scheme* (from 1990) reduced customs duties on goods made in the region, and a Common External Tariff came into force in 2015.
3. Progress in *infrastructure and energy:* the Trans-West African Coastal Highway project, telecommunications links and the West African Power Pool.
4. The ECOWAS Fund (now EBID) has funded development projects, and the *West African Monetary Zone* project aims at a single currency.
*Limits.*
1. Trade among members is still a small part of their total trade (often put at about one tenth), because the economies produce similar raw materials.
2. Poor roads and rail, customs delays, non-tariff barriers and road-block bribes slow trade.
3. Overlapping groupings (such as the CFA franc zone and UEMOA), language differences, delays in paying contributions and Nigeria's dominance weaken integration.
4. Wars (Liberia, Sierra Leone, Ivory Coast) and later coups drained resources and attention; some members have expelled migrants (for example Nigeria in 1983 and 1985), contrary to free movement.

**Conclusion.** ECOWAS has made real progress in free movement and in building institutions, but it has so far achieved only a part of its economic aims; poverty, poor infrastructure and political instability remain.
